papers.title: Ultraviolet Reflected-Light Spectroscopy of Modern Earth Analogs with Starshade Observations
papers.abstract: Characterizing rocky, habitable zone planets in reflected light is a key science objective for future direct imaging missions, and the ultraviolet (UV) is uniquely suited for supporting the characterization of Earth-like atmospheres. The Hartley-Huggins ozone band at 0.25 μm remains detectable at low spectral resolution down to 0.1\% PAL O₂, providing a sensitive proxy for oxygen-bearing chemistry even for Proterozoic-like atmospheres where the visible and near-infrared O₂ features become inaccessible. This work uses an end-to-end framework for UV starshade spectroscopy of modern Earth analogs that integrates high-fidelity observation simulation, conservative post-processing, and Bayesian spectral retrieval to quantify ozone detection significance. The framework is applied across 108 simulated scenes spanning a range of planet phase angles, system inclinations, and exozodiacal dust densities. The results establish that robust ozone detection with UV-only, R=7 reflected light spectroscopy requires a photometric SNR 30. UV starshade observations with the Habitable Worlds Observatory achieve this threshold within 3-day integrations for solar-type systems at 10 parsecs with inclinations up to 60′ at favorable phases (≤ 90′). Above this SNR threshold, ozone detections are robust to systematic bias from imperfect exozodi calibration within 30\%, and the median retrieved ozone abundance remains accurate to within one order of magnitude of the true value.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
One of astronomy's biggest goals is to study Earth-sized planets around other stars and look for signs of life-friendly chemistry. Oxygen is a key clue, but the usual oxygen fingerprints in visible and near-infrared light fade when a planet has much less oxygen than today's Earth, as ours did for much of its history. Ultraviolet (UV) light offers a backup. Ozone, the molecule made from oxygen that forms our planet's sunscreen layer, absorbs strongly near 0.25 micrometers. This feature stays detectable even at 0.1% of present-day oxygen levels.

**What They Did**
The team built a complete simulated pipeline for a "starshade," a giant flower-shaped screen flown far in front of a space telescope to block a star's glare, so a faint planet next to it can be seen. The pipeline simulates the observation, cleans the data cautiously, and then uses a statistical method called Bayesian retrieval to judge how confidently ozone is detected. They tested 108 simulated scenes with different planet phases (how much of the planet is lit, like the Moon's phases), different tilts of the planetary system, and different amounts of exozodiacal dust, the dust in a planetary system that glows and acts like fog around the planet.

**Key Findings**
Using only very coarse UV color information (resolution R=7, roughly a handful of broad colors), a reliable ozone detection needs a photometric signal-to-noise ratio of about 30, meaning the planet's signal is roughly 30 times the noise. The Habitable Worlds Observatory could reach this in 3-day exposures for a Sun-like star 10 parsecs (about 33 light-years) away, with system tilts up to 60 degrees and favorable phases up to 90 degrees. Above that threshold, detections held up even if the dust glow was mis-estimated by up to 30%. The median ozone amount recovered was within a factor of ten of the true value.

**Looking Forward**
These results give mission planners a concrete signal-quality target for UV observations of Earth-like worlds. They also show that ozone could be a useful oxygen clue even for planets whose oxygen is too scarce to show up at longer wavelengths.

papers.title_tr: Starshade Gözlemleriyle Modern Dünya Benzerlerinin Ultraviyole Yansıyan Işık Tayfölçümü
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Gökbilimin en büyük hedeflerinden biri, başka yıldızların çevresindeki Dünya boyutlu gezegenleri incelemek ve yaşama elverişli kimyanın izlerini aramaktır. Oksijen önemli bir ipucudur. Ancak bir gezegende oksijen bugünkü Dünya'dakinden çok daha azsa, görünür ve yakın kızılötesi ışıktaki olağan oksijen izleri silikleşir. Dünya da tarihinin büyük bölümünde böyle bir dönemden geçti. Ultraviyole (UV) ışık burada bir yedek sunar. Gezegenimizin güneş koruyucu tabakasını oluşturan ve oksijenden meydana gelen ozon molekülü, 0,25 mikrometre civarında güçlü biçimde ışık soğurur. Bu özellik, bugünkü oksijen düzeyinin yüzde 0,1'ine inildiğinde bile tespit edilebilir durumda kalır.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Ekip, bir "starshade" için uçtan uca bir benzetim hattı kurdu. Starshade, bir uzay teleskobunun önünde çok uzakta uçan, çiçek biçimli dev bir perdedir. Yıldızın göz kamaştırıcı ışığını keserek yanındaki sönük gezegenin görülmesini sağlar. Hat, gözlemi benzetim yoluyla üretir, veriyi temkinli biçimde temizler, ardından Bayesçi geri çatım (retrieval) adı verilen istatistiksel bir yöntemle ozonun ne kadar güvenle tespit edildiğini değerlendirir. Ekip 108 benzetim sahnesini sınadı. Bu sahnelerde gezegenin faz açısı (Ay'ın evreleri gibi, gezegenin ne kadarının aydınlık olduğu), gezegen sisteminin eğikliği ve ekzozodiyakal toz miktarı değişiyordu. Ekzozodiyakal toz, gezegen sistemindeki parlayan ve gezegenin çevresinde sis gibi davranan tozdur.

**Ana Bulgular**
Yalnızca çok kaba UV renk bilgisiyle (R=7 çözünürlük, yani kabaca birkaç geniş renk bandı) güvenilir bir ozon tespiti için yaklaşık 30 veya daha yüksek bir fotometrik sinyal-gürültü oranı gerekir. Bu, gezegenin sinyalinin gürültüden yaklaşık 30 kat güçlü olması demektir. Habitable Worlds Observatory, 10 parsek (yaklaşık 33 ışık yılı) uzaktaki Güneş benzeri bir yıldız için bu düzeye 3 günlük pozlamalarla ulaşabilir. Bunun için sistem eğikliğinin 60 dereceye kadar, uygun fazların ise 90 dereceye kadar olması yeterlidir. Bu eşiğin üzerinde, toz parıltısı yüzde 30'a kadar yanlış kestirilse bile tespitler sağlam kalmıştır. Elde edilen ozon miktarının ortancası gerçek değerin on katı içinde kalmıştır.

**İleriye Bakış**
Bu sonuçlar, görev planlamacılarına Dünya benzeri gezegenlerin UV gözlemleri için somut bir sinyal kalitesi hedefi verir. Ayrıca ozonun, oksijeni daha uzun dalga boylarında görünemeyecek kadar az olan gezegenler için bile işe yarar bir oksijen ipucu olabileceğini gösterir.

papers.title: Simulations of the Evolving Ozone Layer: Implications for the Early Earth, Exoplanets, and the Search For Life
papers.abstract: Over 4 billion years, Earth's atmosphere has been transformed from a composition devoid of molecular oxygen (O₂) to one where O₂ is now 21% of our modern atmosphere by volume. With high quantities of O₂, an ozone (O₃) layer can form and partially shield the surface from biologically harmful ultraviolet radiation (UV). The evolution of the O₃ layer has previously been simulated under the modern Sun by independent groups with separate models. Here, we present simulations of Earth's atmosphere from four open-source one-dimensional (1D) photochemical models and a 3D chemistry-climate model, focussing on O₃. We find that the O₃ layer thickness exhibits a clear deviation between the 1D models and the 3D model due to several factors, including treatments of O₂ photolysis, chemical networks, H₂O microphysics and 3D transport. We find that 1D models introduce a bias for unobserved climate states and show how these biases may propagate to calculations of biological UV damage and surface habitability. We show that when applied to specific exoplanet atmospheres, these discrepancies can become more pronounced, propagating through to observational predictions for the next generation of telescopes, such as HWO and LIFE, that will search for habitable and inhabited exoplanets.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
For most of Earth's history, the air held almost no free oxygen. Today oxygen makes up 21% of the atmosphere by volume. That change allowed an ozone layer to form, a thin veil of gas high above us that works like planetary sunscreen, absorbing much of the harmful ultraviolet (UV) light from the Sun. Ozone is also one of the gases astronomers hope to detect on distant planets as a possible sign of oxygen, and perhaps life. To read those signals correctly, we need computer models of ozone that we can trust.

**What They Did**
Earlier studies simulated how the ozone layer evolved over Earth's history, but separate research groups used separate models, so the results were hard to compare. In this work, the team ran simulations of Earth's atmosphere in four open-source one-dimensional (1D) photochemical models and one three-dimensional (3D) chemistry-climate model. A 1D model treats the atmosphere as a single column of air, like a core sample. A 3D model covers the whole globe, including winds and circulation. All the simulations assumed the modern Sun, and the team focused on ozone.

**Key Findings**
The thickness of the ozone layer differed clearly between the 1D models and the 3D model. The authors trace this to several factors: how each model handles the splitting of oxygen molecules by sunlight, the lists of chemical reactions used, how water droplets and ice are treated, and the way air moves around the globe in 3D. They also find that 1D models can introduce a bias for climate states that have never been observed. That bias can carry through to estimates of biological UV damage and surface habitability. When the models were applied to specific exoplanet atmospheres, the differences became even larger.

**Looking Forward**
These discrepancies affect the predictions that guide the next generation of space telescopes, such as the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) and the Large Interferometer For Exoplanets (LIFE). Both are designed to search for habitable and inhabited worlds. The results suggest that interpreting the ozone signals they detect will require careful, cross-checked modelling that accounts for each model's limitations.

papers.title_tr: Evrimleşen Ozon Tabakasının Simülasyonları: Erken Dünya, Ötegezegenler ve Yaşam Arayışı İçin Çıkarımlar
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Dünya'nın tarihinin büyük bölümünde havada serbest oksijen neredeyse hiç yoktu. Bugün ise oksijen, atmosferin hacimce %21'ini oluşturuyor. Bu değişim bir ozon tabakasının oluşmasını sağladı. Ozon tabakası, tepemizde yer alan ince bir gaz perdesidir ve gezegenin güneş kremi gibi çalışarak Güneş'ten gelen zararlı morötesi (UV) ışığın büyük bölümünü soğurur. Ozon aynı zamanda gökbilimcilerin uzak gezegenlerde bulmayı umduğu, oksijenin ve belki de yaşamın olası bir işareti olan gazlardan biridir. Bu sinyalleri doğru yorumlayabilmek için ozon konusunda güvenebileceğimiz bilgisayar modellerine ihtiyaç var.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Önceki çalışmalar Dünya tarihi boyunca ozon tabakasının nasıl evrildiğini simüle etti. Ancak farklı araştırma grupları farklı modeller kullandığı için sonuçları karşılaştırmak zordu. Bu çalışmada ekip, Dünya atmosferinin simülasyonlarını dört açık kaynaklı tek boyutlu (1B) fotokimyasal modelle ve bir üç boyutlu (3B) kimya-iklim modeliyle yaptı. Tek boyutlu model atmosferi, tıpkı bir karot örneği gibi tek bir hava sütunu olarak ele alır. Üç boyutlu model ise rüzgârlar ve dolaşım dahil olmak üzere tüm küreyi kapsar. Tüm simülasyonlarda günümüzün Güneş'i esas alındı ve ekip ozona odaklandı.

**Ana Bulgular**
Ozon tabakasının kalınlığı, 1B modeller ile 3B model arasında belirgin biçimde farklıydı. Yazarlar bu farkı birkaç etkene bağlıyor: her modelin oksijen moleküllerinin güneş ışığıyla parçalanmasını ele alış biçimi, kullanılan kimyasal tepkime listeleri, su damlacıkları ve buzun nasıl işlendiği ve 3B modelde havanın küre çevresinde hareketi. Ayrıca 1B modellerin, hiç gözlenmemiş iklim durumları için bir yanlılık getirebildiğini buluyorlar. Bu yanlılık, biyolojik UV hasarı ve yüzeyin yaşanabilirliği tahminlerine de yansıyabilir. Modeller belirli ötegezegen atmosferlerine uygulandığında ise farklar daha da büyüdü.

**İleriye Bakış**
Bu tutarsızlıklar, Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) ve Large Interferometer For Exoplanets (LIFE) gibi yeni nesil uzay teleskoplarına yön veren tahminleri etkiliyor. Her iki teleskop da yaşanabilir ve yaşam barındıran dünyaları aramak için tasarlandı. Sonuçlar, bu teleskopların saptayacağı ozon sinyallerini yorumlamak için, her modelin sınırlarını hesaba katan ve birbiriyle karşılaştırılarak doğrulanmış dikkatli bir modellemeye ihtiyaç duyulacağını gösteriyor.

papers.title: High-resolution transmission spectroscopy of KELT-18b Metastable helium detection at 1083 nm
papers.abstract: We present the first high-resolution transmission spectroscopy of the ultrahot Jupiter KELT-18b, probing its escaping atmosphere by analyzing a single transit obtained with the CARMENES spectrograph. Transmission spectroscopy and Doppler tomography were utilized to isolate the planetary signal. To mitigate contamination from the strong telluric OH lines overlapping the region of interest, two distinct data analysis procedures were applied: a standard Molecfit and OH-masking approach as well as a PCA-based method. By combining the two complementary approaches, we successfully detect a He\,I triplet absorption feature of 1.10 ± 0.22\% (5.1σ). The signal exhibits a velocity shift consistent with zero and is attributed to the exoplanetary atmosphere. An injection test reveals that the PCA-based method significantly suppresses the retrieved signal. Additionally, using the ATES and TPM codes, we modeled the atmospheric photoevaporation and the helium triplet profile for different He/H ratios and stellar XUV fluxes, accounting for instrument and planetary rotational broadening. From our simulations we derive a mass-loss rate and an evaporation efficiency for KELT-18b of 10.47 ≤ ₁₀(M) ≤ 11.68 and 0.153 ≤ η≤ 0.321, demonstrating that the atmosphere of KELT-18b is undergoing photoevaporation. Furthermore, our simulations show good agreement with the observed transmission spectrum, allowing us to exclude very low He/H ratios at a 3σ confidence level for XUV fluxes up to approximately twice the nominal reconstructed value. Our result expands the known parameter space of exoplanets with confirmed helium absorption, establishing KELT-18b as the most massive planet orbiting the hottest host star with such a detection.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Some planets orbit so close to their stars that they are slowly being stripped of their atmospheres, much like a snowball melting in the sun. KELT-18b is one of these "ultrahot Jupiters", a gas giant heated to extreme temperatures by a very hot star. Astronomers want to know how fast such planets lose gas, because that loss can reshape a planet over billions of years. One of the best tracers of escaping gas is helium, which absorbs a very specific color of infrared light (at 1083 nanometers). Until now, nobody had looked for it around KELT-18b.

**What They Did**
The team watched a single transit, the moment the planet passes in front of its star, using the CARMENES spectrograph, an instrument that splits starlight into fine detail. They looked for starlight dimmed by helium in the planet's atmosphere. The signal is hard to find because Earth's own atmosphere glows with interfering "OH" lines at nearly the same wavelengths. So the researchers used two different cleaning methods: one that models and masks the contamination, and a statistical method called principal component analysis (PCA). papers.title_tr: KELT-18b'nin yüksek çözünürlüklü geçiş tayfölçümü: 1083 nm'de kararlı (metastable) helyum tespiti
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Bazı gezegenler yıldızlarına o kadar yakın dönerler ki atmosferleri, güneşte eriyen bir kartopu gibi yavaş yavaş soyulur. Gökbilimciler bu tür gezegenlerin ne kadar hızlı gaz kaybettiğini bilmek ister, çünkü bu kayıp milyarlarca yıl içinde gezegenin yapısını değiştirebilir. Kaçan gazın en iyi izleyicilerinden biri, kızılötesi ışığın çok belirli bir rengini (1083 nanometre) soğuran helyumdur. Şimdiye kadar KELT-18b çevresinde helyum aranmamıştı.

Ekip, gezegenin yıldızının önünden geçtiği anı, yani tek bir geçişi, ışığı ince ayrıntılarına ayıran CARMENES tayfçekeriyle gözlemledi. Gezegenin atmosferindeki helyum nedeniyle yıldız ışığında oluşan sönümlenmeyi aradılar. Sinyali bulmak zordur, çünkü Dünya'nın kendi atmosferindeki "OH" çizgileri neredeyse aynı dalga boylarında parazit yapar. Araştırmacılar bu yüzden iki farklı temizleme yöntemi kullandı: biri kirlenmeyi modelleyip maskeliyor, diğeri ise temel bileşen analizi (PCA) adlı istatistiksel bir yöntemdi. Ayrıca farklı helyum/hidrojen oranlarını ve yıldızın yüksek enerjili ışınım düzeylerini deneyerek gezegen atmosferinin bilgisayar benzetimlerini yaptılar.

**Ana Bulgular**
Yüzde 1,10 ± 0,22 oranında helyum soğurması saptadılar (5,1 sigma); bu, tesadüf olma ihtimalinin çok düşük olduğu anlamına gelir. Benzetimler, gezegenin foto-buharlaşma yoluyla kütle kaybettiğini ve verimliliğin yaklaşık yüzde 15 ile 32 arasında olduğunu gösteriyor. Bu sonuç yalnızca tek bir geçişe dayanıyor; bu yüzden ayrıntıları doğrulamak için daha fazla gözlem yararlı olacaktır. Çalışma, helyum kaçışının bilindiği gezegenlerin aralığını genişletiyor ve sıcak yıldızların çevresinde atmosfer kaybının nasıl işlediğini sınamaya yardımcı oluyor.

papers.title: Dynamically Coupled Three-dimensional Cloud-Chemistry in Rapidly Rotating Irradiated Atmospheres: an Application to the Compact White Dwarf-Brown Dwarf system ZTFJ0038+2030
papers.abstract: Clouds and disequilibrium chemistry shape the observable properties of substellar and planetary atmospheres, and JWST time-resolved spectroscopy now enables direct tests of their three-dimensional structures. We present an update to the 3D atmospheric framework ADAM, coupling the dynamical core to a miniature kinetic chemistry scheme (mini-chem) and a saturation-relaxation tracer cloud module. Using this framework, we investigate the atmosphere of the brown dwarf orbiting the white dwarf ZTFJ0038+2030 in a 10-hour orbit. The brown dwarf receives stellar irradiation comparable to its internal heat flux, placing the atmosphere in a regime where the circulation is characterized by a standing Matsuno--Gill wave response and equatorial superrotation. Rapid rotation confines these structures closer to the equator, producing more symmetric broadband light curves with smaller hotspot offsets than canonical hot Jupiters, in agreement with recent JWST observations of this system. Although most species are globally homogenized, rapid rotation limits global-scale horizontal mixing and allows circulation-driven vertical transport to maintain strong CO and CO₂ inhomogeneities in the photosphere. These chemical inhomogeneities produce asymmetric phase curves in the CO and CO₂ absorption bands, which could qualitatively explain the observed CO₂ light-curve asymmetry. When clouds are included, Na₂S clouds dominate the photosphere and weaken the large-scale circulation, lowering photospheric CO and CO₂ abundances, while MgSiO₃ and Fe clouds rain out at deeper levels. Because the dominant Na₂S clouds reside mostly above the quench region, cloud-driven convection has limited impact on the quenched abundances, which are instead regulated mainly by large-scale circulation.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Imagine a world where one side is blasted by light from a dead star while the other side stays dark, and the whole planet-sized object spins once every 10 hours. That is the brown dwarf orbiting the white dwarf ZTFJ0038+2030. A brown dwarf is an object too small to be a true star but bigger than a planet. Clouds and shifting chemistry shape what telescopes can see in such atmospheres. The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) can now watch these objects rotate and track how their brightness changes, so we can test ideas about their weather in three dimensions.

**What They Did**
The team upgraded a computer weather model called ADAM. They added a simplified chemistry scheme that tracks how gases such as carbon monoxide (CO) and carbon dioxide (CO₂) are made and destroyed. They also added a simple cloud scheme in which vapor condenses into cloud and then rains out. They then simulated the brown dwarf's atmosphere. It receives starlight about as strong as its own internal heat.

**Key Findings**
Fast rotation squeezes the main wind patterns toward the equator, much as a spinning top keeps its motion tight around its middle. As a result, the brightness changes as the object orbits are more symmetric, and the hottest spot is shifted less than on typical "hot Jupiters." This matches the JWST observations. Most gases are mixed evenly around the globe. CO and CO₂ are the exception: winds carry them up and down faster than rapid rotation lets them spread sideways, so they stay patchy. This could help explain a lopsided CO₂ signal seen by JWST. Clouds of sodium sulfide (Na₂S) dominate the visible layers and weaken the winds, which lowers CO and CO₂. Magnesium silicate and iron clouds sit deeper down. Because the sodium sulfide clouds lie mostly above the layer where the chemistry gets "frozen in," cloud-driven stirring has little effect on the CO and CO₂ amounts. Large-scale circulation sets those instead.

**Looking Forward**
These predictions give astronomers specific patterns to look for in JWST data. They also offer a way to test whether such models can describe other fast-spinning, irradiated worlds.

papers.title_tr: Hızlı Dönen, Işınlanan Atmosferlerde Dinamik Olarak Eşleşmiş Üç Boyutlu Bulut-Kimya: Sıkı Beyaz Cüce-Kahverengi Cüce Sistemi ZTFJ0038+2030 Üzerine Bir Uygulama
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Bir yanı ölü bir yıldızın ışığıyla kavrulurken diğer yanı karanlıkta kalan ve her 10 saatte bir kendi etrafında dönen bir dünya düşünün. ZTFJ0038+2030 sistemindeki beyaz cücenin yörüngesinde dolanan kahverengi cüce tam olarak böyle bir nesne. Kahverengi cüce, gerçek bir yıldız olamayacak kadar küçük, ancak bir gezegenden büyük bir gök cismidir. Bulutlar ve değişen kimya, bu tür atmosferlerde teleskopların gördüklerini belirler. James Webb Uzay Teleskobu (JWST) artık bu nesnelerin dönüşünü izleyip parlaklık değişimlerini takip edebiliyor. Böylece bu atmosferlerin üç boyutlu havasıyla ilgili fikirler sınanabiliyor.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Ekip, ADAM adlı bir bilgisayar hava durumu modelini geliştirdi. Modele, karbon monoksit (CO) ve karbondioksit (CO₂) gibi gazların nasıl oluştuğunu ve yok olduğunu izleyen basitleştirilmiş bir kimya şeması ekledi. Ayrıca buharın yoğuşup bulut oluşturduğu ve ardından yağmur olarak düştüğü basit bir bulut şeması da eklediler. Sonra kahverengi cücenin atmosferini simüle ettiler. Bu cisim, kendi iç ısısına yakın şiddette yıldız ışığı alıyor.

**Ana Bulgular**
Hızlı dönüş, ana rüzgâr desenlerini ekvatora doğru sıkıştırıyor. Bu, dönen bir topacın hareketinin orta kısmında toplanmasına benzer. Sonuçta yörünge boyunca parlaklık değişimleri daha simetrik oluyor ve en sıcak nokta, tipik "sıcak Jüpiterlere" göre daha az kayıyor. Bu durum JWST gözlemleriyle uyumlu. Gazların çoğu küre boyunca eşit biçimde karışıyor. CO ve CO₂ bunun dışında kalıyor: rüzgârlar bu gazları, hızlı dönüşün yanlara yayılmalarına izin verdiğinden daha hızlı yukarı ve aşağı taşıyor, bu yüzden dağılımları düzensiz kalıyor. Bu, JWST'nin gördüğü dengesiz CO₂ sinyalini açıklamaya yardımcı olabilir. Sodyum sülfür (Na₂S) bulutları görünür katmanlara egemen oluyor ve rüzgârları zayıflatarak CO ile CO₂'yi azaltıyor. Magnezyum silikat ve demir bulutları ise daha derinde duruyor. Sodyum sülfür bulutları çoğunlukla kimyanın "donup kaldığı" katmanın üstünde yer aldığından, bulutların yol açtığı karışımın CO ve CO₂ miktarları üzerindeki etkisi az. Bu miktarları büyük ölçekli dolaşım belirliyor.

**İleriye Bakış**
Bu öngörüler, gökbilimcilere JWST verilerinde aramaları için belirli desenler sunuyor. Ayrıca bu tür modellerin hızlı dönen ve ışınlanan diğer dünyaları açıklayıp açıklayamayacağını sınamanın bir yolunu gösteriyor.

papers.title: TESS Pulsation Timing Reveals the JWST Calibration Star HD 158485 as a Double-pulsator Binary
papers.abstract: HD 158485 is an A-type δ Scuti star in the CALSPEC network and the JWST absolute-flux calibration program. Gaia DR3 assigns it a binary classification probability close to unity but provides no orbital solution. Using TESS observations from Sectors 14--26, 40--41, 47--60, and 73--86, we measure the pulsation phases of six δ Scuti modes. The frequencies form two groups with opposite light-travel-time delays, revealing two pulsating components. A direct light-curve forward model yields an orbital period of P ₒrb=382.80⁺⁰.⁸⁰₋₀.₇₆ d, eccentricity e=0.242⁺⁰.⁰⁴⁵₋₀.₀₄₆, projected light-time amplitudes of 195.8⁺⁹.²₋₈.₉ and 239.7⁺⁶.⁸₋₆.₈ s, and a dynamical mass ratio of q=M_B/M_A=0.818⁺⁰.⁰⁴⁶₋₀.₀₄₅. A blind prediction based only on the first two long TESS campaigns reproduces the third campaign without updating the orbital parameters, with a Pearson correlation coefficient of r=0.983. Its held-out rms is 83.8 s, compared with 289.9 s when the period is fixed at 365.25 d. A 5.15-σ Hipparcos--Gaia EDR3 proper-motion anomaly independently indicates unresolved astrometric motion. The unresolved companion can also affect spectrophotometric predictions: a conditional PB2-constrained two-atmosphere model differs from the corresponding single-star atmosphere prediction by 1.6\% over 1--5 μm and 2.5\% over 5--28 μm. HD 158485 therefore shows that a calibration-relevant binary can lack a catalogued orbital solution while two independent pulsation clocks reveal and measure its orbit.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Telescopes need reference points, much like a kitchen scale needs a trusted set of weights. The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) uses a small group of well-studied stars as its "weights" to measure how bright things really are. One of them, HD 158485, was assumed to be a single star. Catalogs from the Gaia mission hinted that it is actually a binary, a pair of stars orbiting each other, but gave no details about the orbit. If a calibration star hides a companion, the light it is expected to give off could be slightly wrong.

**What They Did**
HD 158485 is a delta Scuti star, a type that pulses in brightness like a slow heartbeat. The researchers used years of observations from NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) and tracked six pulsation rhythms. When a star orbits a companion, its light arrives a little earlier or later depending on where it is in the orbit, so the pulses drift out of step. The six rhythms split into two groups that drifted in opposite directions. That means both stars pulsate, and each acts as its own clock. The team then fitted the orbit directly to the light curve, the record of brightness over time.

**Key Findings**
The stars orbit each other every 382.80 days, on a moderately stretched orbit (eccentricity 0.242). The light-travel delays were about 196 and 240 seconds, and the second star is about 0.82 times as massive as the first. As a test, the team used only the first two long TESS campaigns to predict the third without adjusting anything. The prediction matched closely (correlation 0.983, typical error 83.8 seconds). Assuming a one-year orbit instead gave an error of 289.9 seconds. Independent evidence from the star's motion across the sky (Hipparcos and Gaia) also points to an unseen companion. Modeling the companion changes predicted infrared brightness by about 1.6% at 1–5 micrometers and 2.5% at 5–28 micrometers.

**Looking Forward**
This shows that pulsating stars can reveal hidden binaries even when catalogs lack an orbit. Calibration stars may deserve this kind of check, so that small hidden effects do not slip into precision measurements.

HD 158485 is a delta Scuti star, a type that pulses in brightness like a slow heartbeat. The researchers used years of observations from NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) and tracked six pulsation rhythms. When a star orbits a companion, its light arrives a little earlier or later depending on where it is in the orbit, so the pulses drift out of step. The six rhythms split into two groups that drifted in opposite directions. That means both stars pulsate, and each acts as its own clock. The team then fitted the orbit directly to the light curve, the record of brightness over time.

Key Findings

The stars orbit each other every 382.80 days, on a moderately stretched orbit (eccentricity 0.242). The light-travel delays were about 196 and 240 seconds, and the second star is about 0.82 times as massive as the first. As a test, the team used only the first two long TESS campaigns to predict the third without adjusting anything. The prediction matched closely (correlation 0.983, typical error 83.8 seconds). Assuming a one-year orbit instead gave an error of 289.9 seconds. Independent evidence from the star's motion across the sky (Hipparcos and Gaia) also points to an unseen companion. Modeling the companion changes predicted infrared brightness by about 1.6% at 1–5 micrometers and 2.5% at 5–28 micrometers.

Looking Forward

This shows that pulsating stars can reveal hidden binaries even when catalogs lack an orbit. Calibration stars may deserve this kind of check, so that small hidden effects do not slip into precision measurements.

Ekip bir sınama yaptı: yalnızca ilk iki uzun TESS dönemini kullanarak hiçbir şeyi ayarlamadan üçüncü dönemi öngördü. Tahmin yakından örtüştü (korelasyon 0,983, tipik hata 83,8 saniye). papers.title: Extinction by non-spherical particles with the Nanoparticle Transition Matrix Code: perspectives for interstellar medium and exoplanetary atmospheres
papers.abstract: The Transition Matrix formalism (T-matrix) offers an optimal solution to the problem of radiation scattering and absorption by particles characterized by a high degree of chemical and structural complexity. However, its application to particle models composed by large numbers of constituents has been classically limited by the substantial computational burden of the method. As a consequence, the investigation of light scattering and absorption processes, in cases where particle asymmetry and non-homogeneity play an important role, typically need to rely on simplifying assumptions which affect the correct interpretation of transmission spectra and extinction curves. This problem has a huge impact on many fields of scientific application. In particular, it has a critical role in astrophysics, because the ability to model highly non homogeneous particles is a fundamental requirement to understand the role of extinction in different phases of the interstellar medium (ISM), as well as to probe the physics of light transmission in planetary atmospheres within the Solar System and beyond. In this work we describe the application of a new implementation of the T-matrix formalism, based on the framework originally developed by Borghese, Denti & Saija and named Nano-particle Transition Matrix code, which leverages the power of modern hardware architectures to reduce the computational costs related to the solution of relevant particle models for the investigation of dust in the ISM and of hot-Jupyter class planets atmospheric aerosols. This new implementation of the T-matrix formalism can handle calculations of increasing complexity with a direct impact in the interpretation of the transmission spectra of transiting exoplanets produced by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and of those expected from the Atmospheric Remote-sensing Infrared Exoplanet Large survey (ARIEL).
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
When starlight passes through a cloud of cosmic dust or the hazy air of a distant planet, the light is dimmed and changed. Some of it is soaked up and some is bounced in new directions. Scientists call this combined dimming "extinction," and reading it correctly tells us what the dust and haze are made of. The trouble is that real cosmic particles are rarely neat little balls. They are lumpy, uneven, and built from many different ingredients. For decades, computing how light interacts with such messy grains has been so demanding that researchers often replaced them with simplified shapes. That shortcut can lead to misreading the data. The problem matters in two places: the dust between the stars, known as the interstellar medium, and the atmospheres of exoplanets, which are planets orbiting other stars.

**What They Did**
The authors describe a new software implementation called the Nano-particle Transition Matrix code. It builds on a mathematical method, the "T-matrix," developed by Borghese, Denti and Saija. Think of the method as a very detailed recipe for how light bounces among all the tiny pieces of one complicated grain. The new code is written to take advantage of modern computer hardware, which cuts the computing cost. This lets it handle particles made of far more components than before. They apply it to models of interstellar dust and to aerosols (tiny floating particles) in the atmospheres of "hot Jupiters," giant planets that orbit very close to their stars.

**Key Findings**
The abstract reports no specific numerical results. Its main claim is that the new implementation can handle calculations of increasing complexity at a lower computational cost. That makes it possible to model highly asymmetric and non-uniform particles without relying on heavy simplifying assumptions.

**Looking Forward**
The authors expect the tool to help interpret transmission spectra, which show how a planet's atmosphere filters starlight as the planet passes in front of its star. These spectra come from the James Webb Space Telescope and will come from the future ARIEL mission, the Atmospheric Remote-sensing Infrared Exoplanet Large survey.

papers.title_tr: Nanoparçacık Geçiş Matrisi Kodu (Nanoparticle Transition Matrix Code) ile küresel olmayan parçacıkların yol açtığı sönümleme: yıldızlararası ortam ve ötegezegen atmosferleri için bakış açıları
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Yıldız ışığı kozmik bir toz bulutundan ya da uzaktaki bir gezegenin puslu atmosferinden geçerken sönükleşir ve değişir. Işığın bir kısmı soğurulur, bir kısmı da yeni yönlere saçılır. Bilim insanları bu toplam sönükleşmeye "sönümleme" der. Sönümlemeyi doğru okumak, toz ve pusun neyden oluştuğunu anlamamızı sağlar. Sorun şu ki gerçek kozmik parçacıklar nadiren düzgün küreler gibidir. Çoğu pürüzlü, düzensiz ve birçok farklı malzemeden oluşmuştur. Onlarca yıldır, ışığın bu tür karmaşık tanelerle etkileşimini hesaplamak o kadar zorlayıcı olmuştur ki araştırmacılar çoğu zaman bu tanelerin yerine basitleştirilmiş şekiller kullanmak zorunda kalmıştır. Bu kısayol verilerin yanlış yorumlanmasına yol açabilir. Konu iki alanda önem taşır: yıldızlar arasındaki toz olan yıldızlararası ortamda ve başka yıldızların etrafında dolanan gezegenler olan ötegezegenlerin atmosferlerinde.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Yazarlar, Nanoparçacık Geçiş Matrisi Kodu (Nano-particle Transition Matrix code) adlı yeni bir yazılım uygulamasını anlatıyor. Kod, Borghese, Denti ve Saija'nın geliştirdiği "T-matrisi" adlı matematiksel yönteme dayanıyor. Bu yöntemi, ışığın karmaşık bir tanenin tüm küçük parçaları arasında nasıl sekeceğini anlatan çok ayrıntılı bir tarif gibi düşünebilirsiniz. Yeni kod, modern bilgisayar donanımından yararlanacak biçimde yazılmıştır ve bu da hesaplama maliyetini düşürür. Böylece daha önce mümkün olandan çok daha fazla bileşenden oluşan parçacıkları ele alabiliyor. Yazarlar kodu, yıldızlararası toz modellerine ve "sıcak Jüpiterler"in atmosferlerindeki aerosollere (havada asılı minik parçacıklara) uyguluyor. Sıcak Jüpiterler, yıldızlarına çok yakın dolanan dev gezegenlerdir.

**Ana Bulgular**
Özet belirli sayısal sonuçlar vermiyor. Ana iddia, yeni uygulamanın giderek karmaşıklaşan hesaplamaları daha düşük hesaplama maliyetiyle yapabilmesidir. Bu sayede, ağır basitleştirici varsayımlara başvurmadan, son derece asimetrik ve homojen olmayan parçacıkları modellemek mümkün oluyor.

**İleriye Bakış**
Yazarlar, aracın geçiş tayflarının yorumlanmasına yardımcı olmasını bekliyor. Bu tayflar, bir gezegen yıldızının önünden geçerken atmosferinin yıldız ışığını nasıl süzdüğünü gösterir. Tayflar James Webb Space Telescope'tan geliyor, gelecekte ise ARIEL görevinden (Atmospheric Remote-sensing Infrared Exoplanet Large survey) gelecek.

papers.title: A Spatial Map of the Atmospheric Limb of a Hot Jupiter
papers.abstract: Planets are inherently three-dimensional objects shaped by their thermal structure and dynamics. Observations of transiting exoplanets have begun to uncover this three-dimensional nature, with JWST measuring their dayside atmosphere structure with eclipse mapping, and exploring spectroscopic asymmetries in the limbs of planets during transit. We apply the novel mapping method of transmission strings to the hot Jupiter WASP-17b. With this method, we are not only able to extract hemispheric limb asymmetries from east-to-west, but can map equator-to-pole variations around the transmitting atmosphere as a function of angle, spanning 0.6-12μm. We find a clear transition in the thermal scale height around the limb of the atmosphere, with a 650K temperature difference between the morning (T=858⁺⁴³⁴₋₂₃₃K) and evening (T=1522⁺¹¹⁶₋₁₁₄K). These results are consistent with both nightside emission and dayside eclipse mapping measurements, and represent a fully comprehensive set of observations for a transiting exoplanet. We are also able to constrain the abundances of H₂O and CO₂ to constant values around the limb, providing observational constraints to results from global circulation models. The transmission string technique combined with the outstanding observability of WASP-17b pushes the study of exoplanet atmospheres further into a three-dimensional understanding of hot Jupiter dynamics and chemistry
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Planets are not flat discs. They are three-dimensional worlds with winds, weather and temperature differences from place to place. Hot Jupiters, giant gas planets that orbit extremely close to their stars, are expected to have especially dramatic contrasts. Astronomers have recently begun to see this 3D nature. The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has mapped the daytime side of such planets and spotted differences between the two edges of their atmospheres as they pass in front of their stars.

**What They Did**
The team applied a new mapping method called "transmission strings" to WASP-17b, a hot Jupiter. During a transit, a little starlight filters through the thin ring of atmosphere around the planet's edge, known as the limb. Earlier approaches could mostly compare the east side with the west. This method can also map changes from the equator toward the poles, at different angles around the ring. The researchers used light spanning 0.6 to 12 micrometres, from visible to infrared wavelengths, so they could study the atmosphere's temperature and chemistry.

**Key Findings**
The limb shows a clear change in temperature. The morning side is about 858 kelvin, with a wide uncertainty (roughly 233 K lower to 434 K higher). The evening side is about 1522 kelvin, with a tighter uncertainty of about 115 K. That is a difference of around 650 kelvin. These results agree with earlier measurements of the planet's glowing nightside and with maps of its dayside. The authors describe the combined picture as a fully comprehensive set of observations for a transiting exoplanet. They also found that the amounts of water (H₂O) and carbon dioxide (CO₂) can be held at constant values around the limb. This gives real observational tests for global circulation models, the computer simulations of a planet's winds and climate.

**Looking Forward**
The transmission string technique, together with how well WASP-17b can be observed, moves the study of exoplanet atmospheres toward a truly three-dimensional view. The goal is to understand both the motion and the chemistry of hot Jupiters, not just their average properties.

papers.title_tr: Bir Sıcak Jüpiter'in Atmosferik Kenarının Mekânsal Haritası
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Gezegenler düz birer disk değildir. Rüzgârları, hava olayları ve bir yerden diğerine değişen sıcaklık farkları olan üç boyutlu dünyalardır. papers.title: The EBLM Project - XIX. The absence of radius inflation in a homogeneous analysis of 66 Northern low-mass eclipsing binaries
papers.abstract: Precise and accurate measurements of host stars are crucial in the search for Earth-like exoplanets, and M-dwarfs are favourable targets in this quest. Low-mass eclipsing binaries offer unique opportunities to empirically determine stellar masses and radii for low-mass stars where stellar models may be systematically biased. We present results from the EBLM-North sample, the largest homogeneous study of low-mass eclipsing binaries with secondary characterisation yet, combining high-resolution and high-precision radial velocities from SOPHIE and TESS photometry. We measure a median precision for stellar companions of 4.2% in radius and 8.6% in mass within a sub-sample of 50 high-quality binaries, all with orbital periods P biₙ > 5\, days. We compare our data to the Baraffe and MIST isochrones, and find our sample is statistically consistent with those models, producing reduced chi-squared values, χ²_ν 1. Our measured radius inflation is 0.3± 1.6% indicating no statistically significant trend. We likewise detect no significant trend with metallicity, despite having the precision to identify such a relationship. As such, our observations do not appear to follow the general metallicity trend predicted in MIST. A χ_ν² 1 indicates the scatter in our results is commensurate with our uncertainties alone. These results constrain the scope for unmodelled effects on the mass-radius relation that would produce radius deviations greater than 4.2%. However, our secondary effective temperatures do not reproduce this high level of agreement with the models, and we do not recover the predicted trends with metallicity.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Small, dim stars called M-dwarfs are popular hunting grounds for Earth-like planets. A planet's size and mass are worked out from its star's, so any error in the star's measurements carries straight into the planet's. It is like measuring a shadow without knowing how tall the lamp is. The computer models used to predict the sizes of small stars might be systematically off, so they need testing against real measurements.

**What They Did**
The team studied 66 "eclipsing binaries" in the northern sky. These are pairs of stars that orbit each other and take turns passing in front of one another, causing regular dips in brightness. They combined two kinds of data. The first was precise radial velocities from the SOPHIE spectrograph, which track how fast the stars move toward and away from us. The second was brightness measurements from TESS (the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite). Together these give each star's mass and radius. The team focused on a high-quality group of 50 systems with orbital periods longer than 5 days. They then compared the results with two widely used sets of stellar models, called Baraffe and MIST.

**Key Findings**
For the low-mass companion stars, the median precision was 4.2% in radius and 8.6% in mass. The data agreed statistically with both sets of models. The measured "radius inflation", meaning how much larger stars appear than predicted, was just 0.3 ± 1.6%, which is no significant effect. The team also found no trend with metallicity (the amount of elements heavier than hydrogen and helium in a star), even though their precision was good enough to spot one. This differs from the metallicity trend predicted by MIST. The scatter in the results matched what the uncertainties alone would produce. This limits how large any unmodelled effect on the mass-radius relationship could be, ruling out deviations bigger than about 4.2%. However, the stars' temperatures did not agree with the models as well as their sizes did.

**Looking Forward**
The sizes of these small stars look reliable, which is good news for planet hunters. The mismatch in temperatures and metallicity trends shows where the stellar models may still need work.

papers.title_tr: EBLM Projesi - XIX. 66 Kuzey Yarımküre Düşük Kütleli Örten Çift Yıldızın Homojen Analizinde Yarıçap Şişmesinin Bulunmaması
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
M cücesi adı verilen küçük ve sönük yıldızlar, Dünya benzeri gezegen arayışında gözde hedeflerdir. Bir gezegenin boyutu ve kütlesi, ev sahibi yıldızın boyutundan ve kütlesinden hesaplanır. Bu yüzden yıldızın ölçümlerindeki bir hata doğrudan gezegene de yansır. Bu, lambanın boyunu bilmeden gölgeyi ölçmeye benzer. Küçük yıldızların boyutlarını öngören bilgisayar modelleri sistematik olarak hatalı olabilir. Bu nedenle modellerin gerçek ölçümlerle sınanması gerekir.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Ekip, kuzey gökyüzündeki 66 "örten çift yıldızı" inceledi. Bunlar birbirinin etrafında dönen ve sırayla birbirinin önünden geçen yıldız çiftleridir. Bu geçişler parlaklıkta düzenli düşüşlere yol açar. Araştırmacılar iki tür veriyi birleştirdi. Birincisi, yıldızların bize doğru ve bizden uzağa ne kadar hızlı hareket ettiğini izleyen SOPHIE tayf ölçerinden alınan hassas radyal hızlardı. İkincisi, TESS'in (Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite, Geçiş Yapan Ötegezegen Araştırma Uydusu) parlaklık ölçümleriydi. Bu veriler birlikte her yıldızın kütlesini ve yarıçapını verir. Ekip, yörünge periyodu 5 günden uzun olan 50 yüksek kaliteli sisteme odaklandı. Ardından sonuçları Baraffe ve MIST adlı, yaygın kullanılan iki yıldız modeli kümesiyle karşılaştırdı.

**Ana Bulgular**
Düşük kütleli eşlikçi yıldızlar için yarıçapta medyan %4,2, kütlede %8,6 hassasiyete ulaşıldı. Veriler her iki model kümesiyle de istatistiksel olarak uyumluydu. Yıldızların öngörülenden ne kadar büyük göründüğünü anlatan "yarıçap şişmesi" yalnızca %0,3 ± 1,6 olarak ölçüldü. Bu, anlamlı bir etki olmadığı anlamına gelir. Ekip ayrıca metalisite (bir yıldızdaki hidrojen ve helyumdan ağır element miktarı) ile bir eğilim bulamadı. Oysa hassasiyetleri böyle bir eğilimi görmeye yetecek düzeydeydi. Bu durum MIST'in öngördüğü metalisite eğiliminden farklıdır. Sonuçlardaki saçılma, yalnızca belirsizliklerden beklenen düzeydeydi. Bu da modellenmemiş etkilerin kütle-yarıçap ilişkisinde yaratabileceği sapmaları sınırlar ve yaklaşık %4,2'den büyük sapmaları dışarıda bırakır. Ancak yıldızların sıcaklıkları, boyutları kadar iyi bir uyum göstermedi.

**İleriye Bakış**
Bu küçük yıldızların boyutları güvenilir görünüyor. Bu, gezegen avcıları için iyi bir haber. Sıcaklıklardaki uyumsuzluk ve metalisite eğilimlerindeki fark ise yıldız modellerinin hâlâ iyileştirilmesi gereken yerleri gösteriyor.

papers.title: Tracing the Influence of Distant companions on Exoplanetary Systems (TIDES) I. Highly Eccentric and Misaligned Binary Companions to Hot Jupiters
papers.abstract: The origin of hot Jupiters remains an open question. A significant fraction reside in binary or multiple star systems, suggesting that stellar companions may play an important role in shaping their present-day architectures. However, the orbits of the vast majority of these stellar companions remain poorly constrained, leaving their role in hot Jupiter evolution an open question. We present the Tracing the Influence of Distant companions on Exoplanetary Systems (TIDES) survey, a campaign to map the orbits of stellar companions in systems hosting hot Jupiters to assess the extent to which binaries play a role in hot Jupiter formation and migration. Here, we introduce our survey design and new orbital fits for the first six systems in our sample---τ Boo, WASP-2, WASP-11, WASP-76, HAT-P-14, and HAT-P-16---by combining previous observations of the stellar companions together with new Keck/NIRC2 imaging and Keck/KPIC relative radial velocities. Among these six systems, the four with the most precisely constrained orbits exhibit high eccentricities (e ≥ 0.8), and three of these systems also display significant planet--binary misalignments (Δi ≥ 20′). This suggests the orbital properties of stellar companions to hot Jupiter host stars are qualitatively different than field binaries and binaries hosting inner transiting small planets. These orbital architectures are consistent with stellar companions shaping the evolution of hot Jupiters, either through high-eccentricity migration or by participating in an earlier episode of dynamical evolution that ultimately led to hot Jupiter formation. Continued orbital monitoring of the full sample will reveal whether outer stellar companions play a causal role in the evolution of hot Jupiters.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Hot Jupiters are giant planets, similar in size to Jupiter, that circle their stars in just a few days, far closer than Mercury is to our Sun. Nobody is sure how they ended up so close, because giant planets are thought to form far from their stars. Many hot Jupiters live in star systems with a second, distant star. Yet the orbits of those companion stars are mostly poorly known, so we can't tell whether they helped drag the planets inward. It's like suspecting a bystander was involved in an event without knowing where they were standing.

**What They Did**
The researchers launched a survey called TIDES (Tracing the Influence of Distant companions on Exoplanetary Systems). Its goal is to map the orbits of companion stars in hot Jupiter systems. This first paper covers six systems: τ Boo, WASP-2, WASP-11, WASP-76, HAT-P-14, and HAT-P-16. They combined older observations with new Keck telescope data. The new data came from sharp infrared images (NIRC2) and from measurements of the companions' motion toward and away from us, made with the Keck Planet Imager and Characterizer (KPIC).

**Key Findings**
Four of the six systems have well-measured companion orbits, and all four are extremely stretched-out ovals. Their eccentricity, a measure of how elongated an orbit is, is 0.8 or higher, where 0 is a perfect circle and 1 is the limit of stretching. Three of these systems also show a misalignment of at least 20 degrees between the planet's orbit and the companion star's orbit. The authors say these orbits differ from those of ordinary double stars and of double-star systems with small planets close to their stars.

**Looking Forward**
These patterns fit the idea that companion stars help shape hot Jupiters. A companion could push a planet onto a stretched orbit that later shrinks, or it could take part in an earlier gravitational upheaval that created the hot Jupiter. The abstract stops short of proving cause and effect. The team plans to keep monitoring the full sample to find out whether the companions truly play a causal role.

papers.title: Rattling Resonant Chains with Dynamical Tides and Parametric Resonance Passage
papers.abstract: Close-in sub-Neptunes are born in mean-motion resonant chains that break apart on a timescale of 100 Myr. If the chains are first ''rattled'' --- have their free eccentricities excited to a few percent --- then breaking occurs on the required timescale. We propose that chains are rattled by internal oscillations tidally driven by the star in the innermost planet. Unlike other proposals, there is no need to invoke any reservoir of planetesimals or external perturbers --- the chain unravels from within. We develop a Hamiltonian theory (and an accompanying toy model) which predicts a parametric instability whereby chain librations exponentially amplify when the tidal forcing frequency equals the sum of the internal mode frequency and the chain libration frequency. We also introduce a new eigenmode solver for rotating planets, MAQAM, that in combination with the evolutionary code ORCHARD enables us to track the frequency evolution of pressure, gravity, and inertial modes in cooling sub-Neptunes. Inertial modes in the gas envelope and fluid mantle can evolve to become momentarily parametrically resonant. Passage through a single parametric resonance can raise the free eccentricities in the chain to a few percent within a few tens of Myrs.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Many of the small planets orbiting close to their stars, called sub-Neptunes, are thought to be born in tidy "chains." In a chain, neighboring planets tug on each other in a steady rhythm, a bit like children on a row of swings pushed in time. Astronomers call this a mean-motion resonance. Yet most older planetary systems are not in such chains, so the chains must break apart, and observations suggest this happens on a timescale of about 100 million years. Computer models show the chains only break on that schedule if they are first "rattled," meaning their orbits are made a few percent more oval than a perfect circle. What does the rattling has been a puzzle.

**What They Did**
The authors propose that the rattling comes from inside the system. The star's gravity can drive internal oscillations in the innermost planet, much as a singer's note can make a wine glass ring. They built a mathematical theory, plus a simplified toy model, predicting a "parametric instability." This is like pumping a swing at just the right moment. It happens when the tidal pushing frequency equals the sum of the planet's internal oscillation frequency and the chain's own wobble frequency. They also created a new computer tool, MAQAM, which calculates the oscillation modes of spinning planets. They combined it with an evolution code called ORCHARD to follow how those modes change as sub-Neptunes cool.

**Key Findings**
As a sub-Neptune cools, the frequencies of its inner oscillations drift. Inertial modes, which are oscillations restored by the planet's rotation, in the gas envelope and fluid mantle can briefly line up with the chain's rhythm. Passing through just one such parametric resonance can raise the orbital oddness, or free eccentricities, of the chain to a few percent within a few tens of millions of years. No hidden reservoir of small bodies or distant perturbing planet is needed. The chain unravels from within.

**Looking Forward**
The work offers a self-contained explanation for why resonant chains break. It also links the interior structure of sub-Neptunes to the architecture of their planetary systems. The abstract does not describe observational tests.

papers.title_tr: Rezonans Zincirlerini Dinamik Gelgitler ve Parametrik Rezonans Geçişiyle Sarsmak
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Yıldızlarına yakın yörüngede dolanan küçük gezegenlerin birçoğu, yani sub-Neptün'ler, düzenli "zincirler" halinde doğar. Böyle bir zincirde komşu gezegenler birbirini sabit bir ritimle çeker; bu, sırayla ve aynı zamanda itilen bir dizi salıncağa benzer. Gökbilimciler buna ortalama hareket rezonansı der. Ancak yaşlı gezegen sistemlerinin çoğu bu tür zincirler halinde değildir; demek ki zincirler zamanla kopuyor ve gözlemler bunun yaklaşık 100 milyon yıllık bir zaman ölçeğinde gerçekleştiğini gösteriyor. Bilgisayar modelleri, zincirlerin ancak önce "sarsılırlarsa" bu takvimle kopabildiğini gösteriyor; yani yörüngelerinin kusursuz bir daireden yüzde birkaç oranında daha oval hale gelmesi gerekiyor. Sarsıntıyı neyin yaptığı ise bir bilmece olarak kalmıştı.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Yazarlar, sarsıntının sistemin içinden geldiğini öneriyor. Yıldızın kütleçekimi, en içteki gezegende iç salınımları tetikleyebilir; tıpkı bir şarkıcının notasının şarap kadehini titreştirmesi gibi. Bir "parametrik kararsızlık" öngören matematiksel bir kuram ve basitleştirilmiş bir oyuncak model geliştirdiler. Bu durum, salıncağı tam doğru anda itmeye benzer. Gelgit zorlama frekansı, gezegenin iç salınım frekansı ile zincirin kendi sallanma frekansının toplamına eşit olduğunda ortaya çıkar. Ayrıca dönen gezegenlerin salınım kiplerini hesaplayan MAQAM adlı yeni bir bilgisayar aracı oluşturdular. Bunu ORCHARD adlı evrim koduyla birleştirerek sub-Neptün'ler soğurken bu kiplerin nasıl değiştiğini izlediler.

**Ana Bulgular**
Bir sub-Neptün soğudukça iç salınımlarının frekansları kayar. Gezegenin dönmesiyle geri çağrılan salınımlar olan eylemsizlik kipleri, gaz zarfında ve akışkan mantoda zincirin ritmiyle kısa süreliğine örtüşebilir. Tek bir parametrik rezonanstan geçmek bile zincirin serbest dış merkezliklerini, yani yörünge kusurunu, birkaç on milyon yıl içinde yüzde birkaç düzeyine çıkarabilir. Gizli bir küçük cisim havuzuna ya da uzaktaki bir gezegene ihtiyaç yoktur. Zincir içeriden çözülür.

**İleriye Bakış**
Bu çalışma, rezonans zincirlerinin neden koptuğuna kendi içinde tutarlı bir açıklama sunuyor. Ayrıca sub-Neptün'lerin iç yapısını gezegen sistemlerinin mimarisiyle ilişkilendiriyor. Özet, gözlemsel sınamaları anlatmıyor.

papers.title: Star spots mimic the proposed abundance signatures of planet formation
papers.abstract: Trends with stellar elemental abundances and condensation temperature have been proposed as a possible tracer of rocky planet formation. Here we present an alternative explanation, where we show that stellar activity (star spots) can also cause apparent abundance changes in refractory elements preferentially over volatile elements. This effect arises naturally from atomic physics: refractory (rocky; high-Tc) elements preferentially have low first-ionization potentials, with strong transitions that are most sensitive to the cooler, magnetically-perturbed spot conditions, making any spot-induced change in line strength correlated with Tc. We re-examine literature on Sun-like stars in the Solar neighborhood and find that the R'HK stellar activity indicator is correlated with the so-called Tc slope: the gradient of chemical abundances with respect to condensation temperature. Using 1D LTE Korg.jl simulations of the Sun with spots of varying size and contrast, we show that a wide range of spot configurations can manifest as abundance patterns that mimic a signal of abundance trends with condensation temperature. Finally, we conduct a line-by-line differential analysis of an ambient Solar spectrum relative to a Solar sunspot umbra to represent an extreme case, where we find that elements with high condensation temperature can show a factor of three (0.5 dex) increase. We discuss implications that stellar activity poses for precision spectroscopy, and provide some direction on how this effect might be mitigated.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
When astronomers measure what a star is made of, they hope to learn about the planets around it. One proposed clue is a pattern in the star's chemistry. Elements that condense into rock at high temperatures, called refractory elements, seem to be slightly depleted in some stars compared with elements that stay gaseous, called volatile ones. Some researchers have suggested this could be a fingerprint of rocky planet formation, as if the star's missing "rock ingredients" were locked up in planets. This paper offers a more mundane explanation that could change how we read those signals.

**What They Did**
The team argues that star spots, the cooler, magnetically disturbed patches like sunspots, can fake this pattern. Refractory elements tend to have atoms that lose an electron easily, and their strongest spectral lines are especially sensitive to the cooler conditions in spots. The researchers first re-examined published data on Sun-like stars near the Sun and compared a stellar activity indicator, R'HK, with the "Tc slope," which describes how measured abundances change with condensation temperature. They then used Korg.jl, a computer code that simulates starlight, to model the Sun with spots of different sizes and contrasts. Finally, they compared the spectrum of the ordinary Sun with that of a sunspot's darkest core, the umbra, line by line.

**Key Findings**
Stellar activity is correlated with the Tc slope in the literature sample. The simulations showed that many different spot setups can produce abundance patterns that look like a condensation-temperature trend. In the extreme sunspot comparison, high-condensation-temperature elements appeared to increase by a factor of three, or 0.5 dex, with no real change in composition.

**Looking Forward**
The authors say stellar activity is a serious concern for precision spectroscopy, the careful study of starlight to measure chemical makeup. Claims linking a star's chemistry to planet formation may need to account for spots. The paper also offers some direction on how to reduce the effect, though the abstract does not give details.

papers.title_tr: Yıldız lekeleri, gezegen oluşumunun önerilen element bolluğu izlerini taklit ediyor
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Gökbilimciler bir yıldızın neyden oluştuğunu ölçerken, çevresindeki gezegenler hakkında da ipuçları yakalamayı umuyor. Önerilen ipuçlarından biri yıldızın kimyasındaki bir örüntü. Yüksek sıcaklıklarda yoğunlaşıp kayaya dönüşen elementler (refrakter elementler), gaz halinde kalan uçucu elementlere kıyasla bazı yıldızlarda biraz eksik görünüyor. Bazı araştırmacılar bunun kayalık gezegen oluşumunun parmak izi olabileceğini öne sürdü; sanki yıldızın "kaya malzemeleri" gezegenlerin içine hapsolmuş gibi. Bu makale, bu sinyalleri nasıl yorumladığımızı değiştirebilecek daha sıradan bir açıklama sunuyor.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Ekip, Güneş lekeleri gibi daha soğuk ve manyetik olarak bozulmuş bölgeler olan yıldız lekelerinin bu örüntüyü taklit edebileceğini savunuyor. Refrakter elementlerin atomları elektron kaybetmeye yatkındır ve en güçlü tayf çizgileri lekelerdeki soğuk koşullara özellikle duyarlıdır. Araştırmacılar önce Güneş benzeri yakın yıldızlara ait yayımlanmış verileri yeniden inceledi. Yıldız aktivite göstergesi R'HK ile, ölçülen bolluğun yoğunlaşma sıcaklığıyla nasıl değiştiğini anlatan "Tc eğimini" karşılaştırdılar. Ardından, yıldız ışığını simüle eden Korg.jl kodunu kullanarak farklı boyut ve karşıtlıkta lekelere sahip bir Güneş'i modellediler. Son olarak sıradan Güneş'in tayfını, bir Güneş lekesinin en karanlık çekirdeği olan gölge (umbra) bölgesinin tayfıyla çizgi çizgi karşılaştırdılar.

**Ana Bulgular**
Literatürdeki örneklemde yıldız aktivitesi ile Tc eğimi arasında bir ilişki var. Simülasyonlar, birçok farklı leke düzenlemesinin yoğunlaşma sıcaklığı eğilimine benzeyen bolluk örüntüleri üretebildiğini gösterdi. Uç durumdaki Güneş lekesi karşılaştırmasında, yüksek yoğunlaşma sıcaklıklı elementler gerçek bir bileşim değişikliği olmadan üç kat (0,5 dex) artmış göründü.

**İleriye Bakış**
Yazarlar, yıldız aktivitesinin hassas tayfölçüm, yani yıldız ışığıyla kimyasal bileşimin dikkatle ölçülmesi için ciddi bir sorun olduğunu belirtiyor. Bir yıldızın kimyasını gezegen oluşumuna bağlayan iddiaların lekeleri hesaba katması gerekebilir. Makale ayrıca bu etkiyi azaltmak için bazı yönlendirmeler sunuyor, ancak özette ayrıntı verilmiyor.

papers.title: Mid-IR Water-Vapor Seeing: Implications for ELT/METIS High-Contrast Imaging from VLTI Data
papers.abstract: Direct imaging and characterization of rocky exoplanets remains one of the central challenges in exoplanetary science. The mid-infrared (mid-IR) offers a favorable high-contrast imaging (HCI) regime, as the planet-star contrast is more moderate than at shorter wavelengths. However, mid-IR observations with extremely large ground-based telescopes (ELTs) are strongly affected by spatio-temporal fluctuations in atmospheric water vapor (WV), which introduce chromatic wavefront errors that are largely invisible to adaptive optics systems operating at shorter wavelengths. This poses a significant challenge for mid-IR HCI instruments such as METIS, which aims to detect thermal emission from rocky exoplanets in the N-band (8--13 μ m). To quantify WV-induced wavefront errors, we analyze K-band fringe-tracker data from the GRAVITY instrument at the VLTI and derive the optical path difference between group-delay and phase-delay measurements. This difference provides a direct measure of the differential WV column density (Σ) above the telescopes. We examine the dependence of the RMS differential WV column density (σ_Σ) on precipitable water vapor (PWV), airmass, seeing, and wind speed across multiple VLTI configurations. Among these parameters, PWV shows the strongest correlation with σ_Σ. We further explore the influence of the vertical PWV distribution on this relationship. Next, we use power-spectral-density analysis to quantify how increasing PWV modulates Σ variability. The wavefront error associated with this phenomenon on ELT scale is approximately 15 nm RMS in the L-band and 175 nm RMS in the N-band, relative to the K-band. These results provide a quantitative framework for assessing and mitigating atmospheric WV effects in next-generation mid-IR HCI instruments.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Finding and studying Earth-like rocky planets around other stars is one of astronomy's biggest challenges, because a planet is billions of times fainter than the star it orbits. In the mid-infrared, a type of light we feel as heat, the contrast between planet and star is gentler than in visible light. That makes it a promising window. A future instrument called METIS, planned for the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT), aims to detect the heat glow of rocky planets in this range. But there is a catch: water vapor in Earth's atmosphere.

**What They Did**
Water vapor bends infrared light differently from the way dry air does. Because it drifts around unevenly, it blurs the view in ways the telescope's correction system, which works at shorter wavelengths, cannot see. Think of heat shimmer over a road that only affects some colors of light. To measure this, the team used data from GRAVITY, an instrument at the Very Large Telescope Interferometer (VLTI) in Chile. They compared two kinds of timing measurements of starlight, called group delay and phase delay. The difference between them reveals how much water vapor sits above the telescopes. They then checked how this varied with total water vapor in the air, the telescope's viewing angle, atmospheric turbulence, and wind speed. They also used a method that breaks the fluctuations down by how quickly they change.

**Key Findings**
Of all the factors they tested, the total amount of water vapor in the air (precipitable water vapor) showed the strongest link to the fluctuations. They also explored how the height at which the vapor sits matters. For a telescope the size of the ELT, the resulting distortion of the light wave is about 15 nanometers (billionths of a meter) in one infrared band (the L-band) and about 175 nanometers in the N-band (8 to 13 micrometers), compared with the K-band.

**Looking Forward**
These numbers give engineers a concrete yardstick for how much water vapor will hamper METIS, and a starting point for designing ways to correct or work around it, bringing images of rocky planets closer to reality.

papers.title_tr: Orta Kızılötesi Su Buharı Seeing'i: VLTI Verilerinden ELT/METIS Yüksek Kontrastlı Görüntüleme için Çıkarımlar
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Başka yıldızların çevresindeki Dünya benzeri kayalık gezegenleri bulmak ve incelemek astronominin en büyük zorluklarından biridir, çünkü bir gezegen yörüngesinde döndüğü yıldızdan milyarlarca kat daha sönüktür. Isı olarak hissettiğimiz bir ışık türü olan orta kızılötesinde, gezegen ile yıldız arasındaki zıtlık (kontrast) görünür ışığa göre daha yumuşaktır. Bu da orta kızılötesini umut verici bir pencere yapar. Aşırı Büyük Teleskop (ELT) için planlanan METIS adlı gelecekteki bir cihaz, kayalık gezegenlerin ısı ışımasını bu aralıkta saptamayı hedefliyor. Ancak bir engel var: Dünya atmosferindeki su buharı.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Su buharı, kızılötesi ışığı kuru havadan farklı biçimde büküyor. Düzensiz biçimde hareket ettiği için, daha kısa dalga boylarında çalışan teleskopun düzeltme sistemi (uyarlamalı optik) bu bozulmaları göremiyor. Yolun üzerindeki sıcak hava titreşimini düşünün; yalnızca bazı renkleri etkiliyor. Araştırmacılar bunu ölçmek için Şili'deki Çok Büyük Teleskop Girişimölçeri'nde (VLTI) bulunan GRAVITY cihazının verilerini kullandılar. Yıldız ışığının grup gecikmesi ve faz gecikmesi denen iki zamanlama ölçümünü karşılaştırdılar. Aradaki fark, teleskopların üzerindeki su buharı miktarını ortaya koyuyor. Ardından bu değişimin havadaki toplam su buharıyla, teleskopun bakış açısıyla, atmosfer türbülansıyla ve rüzgâr hızıyla nasıl değiştiğine baktılar. Ayrıca dalgalanmaları ne kadar hızlı değiştiklerine göre ayrıştıran bir yöntem de kullandılar.

**Ana Bulgular**
Denenen tüm etkenler arasında, havadaki toplam su buharı miktarı (çökeltilebilir su buharı) dalgalanmalarla en güçlü ilişkiyi gösterdi. Buharın bulunduğu yüksekliğin neden önemli olduğunu da incelediler. ELT boyutundaki bir teleskop için ışık dalgasındaki bu bozulma, K bandına göre, bir kızılötesi bandında (L bandı) yaklaşık 15 nanometre (metrenin milyarda biri), N bandında (8-13 mikrometre) ise yaklaşık 175 nanometredir.

**İleriye Bakış**
Bu sayılar, mühendislere su buharının METIS'i ne kadar zorlayacağına dair somut bir ölçüt sunuyor ve bu etkiyi düzeltmek ya da aşmak için yöntem tasarlamaya başlangıç noktası oluşturuyor. Böylece kayalık ötegezegenlerin görüntülerine bir adım daha yaklaşılıyor.

papers.title: The EBLM project - XX. Absolute dynamical masses of five low-mass eclipsing binaries, and an evaluation of mass estimation methods
papers.abstract: Eclipsing binaries consisting of a solar-type primary and an M dwarf secondary are key laboratories to study objects at the bottom of the main sequence. Fundamental parameters of such stars have a direct impact upon exoplanetary studies, as searches for temperate Earth-sized planets focus on M dwarf hosts. Eclipsing binaries are essential to measure these parameters. However for stellar masses < 0.35 M_☉ , few double-lined eclipsing systems are known. Thus, stellar evolution models and empirical relations have had to rely on single-lined eclipsing binaries, for instance those from the EBLM project (Eclipsing Binary - Low Mass). Using high resolution spectroscopy to extract the weak signal of the secondary (flux ratio < 1 per cent in the optical), we transform five more systems from single to double-lined, deriving absolute masses for both stars. We then compare methods typically employed to estimate stellar masses for field stars or single-lined binaries with the absolute dynamical masses we obtain, to assess their accuracy. Our results for SB1 and SB2 analyses are mostly consistent within 1-σ, though we identify a small systematic overestimation of SB1 masses derived from a combination of radial velocities and eclipse photometry. We show that the bias originates from primary radius overestimation during isochronal analysis, wherein the secondary light reduces photometric magnitudes and impacts the recovered radii by modifying the spectral energy distribution. With proper calibration, we can ensure the accuracy of using the full EBLM SB1 sample to constrain mass-radius-luminosity relationships for the smallest, yet most abundant, stars in the Galaxy
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Most stars in our galaxy are small, dim "M dwarfs", and many of the best searches for Earth-sized, temperate planets target them. To understand those planets, we first need to know how heavy and how big their stars are. The most trustworthy way to weigh a star is to watch it orbit a partner in an "eclipsing binary", a pair of stars that pass in front of each other as seen from Earth. But for stars lighter than about 0.35 times the mass of the Sun, very few such pairs have been measured with both stars clearly detected. Scientists have therefore relied on pairs where only the brighter star's motion could be seen, such as those in the EBLM project (Eclipsing Binary – Low Mass).

**What They Did**
The team studied five systems, each a Sun-like star paired with a faint M dwarf. The M dwarf gives off less than 1 per cent of the system's visible light, like trying to hear a whisper next to a loudspeaker. Using high-resolution spectroscopy, which splits light into fine detail, they pulled out the faint companion's signal. This turned each system from "single-lined" into "double-lined", allowing a direct, dynamical measurement of both stars' masses. They then compared these true masses with the estimates that astronomers usually make for single-lined systems and ordinary field stars.

**Key Findings**
Most of the estimates agreed with the directly measured masses within their stated uncertainties (1-σ). However, the team found a small systematic overestimate in masses from the single-lined method that combines radial velocities (the star's back-and-forth motion) with eclipse brightness data. The cause is that the companion's faint light dims the measured brightness slightly and alters the star's colour pattern, which makes the primary star's radius come out too large during the analysis.

**Looking Forward**
With this bias understood and corrected through proper calibration, the large EBLM sample can be used with confidence. It can help map how mass, size and brightness relate in the smallest and most common stars, and so improve our understanding of the planets around them.

papers.title_tr: EBLM projesi - XX. Beş düşük kütleli tutulma çiftinin mutlak dinamik kütleleri ve kütle tahmin yöntemlerinin bir değerlendirmesi
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Galaksimizdeki yıldızların çoğu, küçük ve sönük "M cüceleri"dir ve Dünya boyutundaki, ılıman gezegenleri arayan en iyi çalışmaların birçoğu bu yıldızları hedefler. Bu gezegenleri anlayabilmek için önce yıldızlarının ne kadar ağır ve ne kadar büyük olduğunu bilmemiz gerekir. Bir yıldızı tartmanın en güvenilir yolu, onu bir eşiyle birlikte dönerken izlemektir. Bu, Dünya'dan bakıldığında yıldızların birbirinin önünden geçtiği "tutulma çifti" sistemlerinde mümkündür. Ancak kütlesi Güneş'in yaklaşık 0,35 katından az olan yıldızlar için her iki yıldızın da açıkça görülebildiği çok az sistem ölçülebilmiştir. Bu yüzden bilim insanları, yalnızca parlak yıldızın hareketinin görülebildiği sistemlere, örneğin EBLM (Eclipsing Binary – Low Mass) projesindekilere, güvenmek zorunda kalmıştır.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Ekip, her biri Güneş benzeri bir yıldız ile sönük bir M cücesinden oluşan beş sistemi inceledi. M cücesi, sistemin görünür ışığının yüzde 1'inden azını yayar. Bu, bir hoparlörün yanındaki fısıltıyı duymaya çalışmak gibidir. Işığı ince ayrıntılara ayıran yüksek çözünürlüklü tayf gözlemleri sayesinde bu sönük eşin sinyalini ayıkladılar. Böylece her sistem "tek çizgili" olmaktan çıkıp "çift çizgili" hale geldi ve iki yıldızın kütleleri doğrudan, dinamik olarak ölçülebildi. Ardından bu gerçek kütleleri, tek çizgili sistemler ve sıradan alan yıldızları için genellikle yapılan kütle tahminleriyle karşılaştırdılar.

**Ana Bulgular**
Tahminlerin çoğu, doğrudan ölçülen kütlelerle belirtilen belirsizlik sınırları (1-σ) içinde uyumluydu. Ancak ekip, radyal hızları (yıldızın ileri geri hareketini) tutulma sırasındaki parlaklık verileriyle birleştiren tek çizgili yöntemde, kütlelerin küçük ama sistematik biçimde olduğundan fazla bulunduğunu saptadı. Nedeni şudur: sönük eşin ışığı ölçülen parlaklığı biraz azaltır ve yıldızın renk dağılımını değiştirir. Bu da analiz sırasında ana yıldızın yarıçapının gerçeğinden büyük çıkmasına yol açar.

**İleriye Bakış**
Bu yanlılık anlaşıldığı ve doğru kalibrasyonla düzeltildiği için, geniş EBLM örneği güvenle kullanılabilir. Bu örnek, en küçük ve en yaygın yıldızlarda kütle, boyut ve parlaklık arasındaki ilişkilerin haritalanmasına ve çevrelerindeki gezegenlerin daha iyi anlaşılmasına yardımcı olabilir.

papers.title: Radiation limits on amino acid preservation and chiral measurement at Oxia Planum
papers.abstract: Amino acid enantiomeric excess (EE) is a potential biosignature, but its measurement requires sufficient surviving material as well as preserved chirality. We derive a criterion that separates abundance-limited from racemization-limited preservation and apply it to the Mars Organic Molecule Analyzer (MOMA) on the ExoMars Rosalind Franklin rover. The model combines cosmic-ray and radiogenic doses with laboratory destruction kinetics and assumed ratios of interconversion to destruction rates. For an initially homochiral population of 1000 ppmw, the surviving EE is 58\% or 25\% when the total abundance reaches 1 ppmw for rate ratios of 0.04 or 0.10, respectively. This abundance criterion does not ensure that both enantiomers can be quantified. Applying provisional estimates of 1 ppmw per enantiomer and 10\% EE, serine at 2 m requires initial concentrations of 340 and 960 ppmw after cosmic-ray exposures of 10⁷ and 10⁸ yr, respectively, under transferred fused-silica--perchlorate kinetics and a 1.57-MGy radiogenic dose. These concentrations exceed measured meteoritic serine abundances, but do not predict the initial Oxia inventory. For organics retained in a closed host since deposition 3.9 Ga ago, the modeled radiogenic dose is 1.6--5.6 MGy across the adopted compositions. In the lower-dose case, drilling to 2 m reduces the total dose by only a factor of 1.5 after 10⁷ yr. The boundaries depend on mineral kinetics and organic residence time; they distinguish preserved chirality from a measurable excess.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Life on Earth builds its proteins almost entirely from "left-handed" amino acids. These molecules come in mirror-image forms, like left and right gloves. Finding a lopsided mix on Mars could hint at biology. But radiation slowly destroys amino acids and also scrambles their handedness, so an ancient signal might fade before anyone can read it.

**What They Did**
The researchers asked when a measurement is limited by too little surviving material and when it is limited by scrambled handedness. They built a model for the Mars Organic Molecule Analyzer (MOMA), an instrument on the ExoMars Rosalind Franklin rover, which is bound for Oxia Planum. The model adds up radiation doses from cosmic rays (fast particles from space) and from radioactive elements in the rock. It then applies laboratory measurements of how quickly amino acids break down, plus assumed ratios between scrambling and destruction rates.

**Key Findings**
Suppose a population starts perfectly one-handed at 1000 parts per million by weight (ppmw). When the total falls to 1 ppmw, the remaining imbalance is 58% or 25%, for scrambling-to-destruction ratios of 0.04 or 0.10. But having 1 ppmw in total does not guarantee that both mirror forms can be measured. The team applied provisional thresholds of 1 ppmw per form and a 10% imbalance. Serine at 2 meters depth would then need to start at 340 ppmw after 10 million years of cosmic-ray exposure, or 960 ppmw after 100 million years. This assumes a radioactive dose of 1.57 megagray. Those starting amounts exceed serine levels measured in meteorites, though they do not predict what Oxia actually held. For organics sealed in rock since 3.9 billion years ago, the modeled radioactive dose is 1.6–5.6 megagray. In the lower-dose case, drilling to 2 meters reduces the total dose by only a factor of 1.5 after 10 million years.

**Looking Forward**
These limits depend on how amino acids behave in particular minerals and on how long the organics have resided in the rock. The authors stress that preserved handedness is not the same as a measurable excess. Both the survival of the molecules and the sensitivity of the measurement matter when judging what the rover could detect.
